title: Icepack: bring your own Python script
chapter_timing: Receipt-bound logical chapters include control cue, actual transition and confirmation; durations are video times.

steps.title: Your goal: run your own Icepack script
instructions: Run a short Python shelf experiment, inspect its fields and save a complete results ZIP.
Have run.py, validate_dataset.py and icepack-shelf-small-v1.json ready.
Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
steps.why: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package. Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.
steps.expected: Your workspace keeps scripts, datasets, run history and results together.
steps.note: Start with your approved cloud account connected and its resources prepared. Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.

steps.title: 1. Open an Advanced workspace
instructions: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack.
You will keep this custom experiment in its own editable workspace.
steps.why: Choose the intended interface, model and example before editing or launching a run.
steps.expected: Use a separate editable workspace for your script.
steps.note: This short 10 km shelf experiment is separate from the canonical spin-up example.

steps.title: 2. Create your workspace example
instructions: Enter a new name, then choose New example.
Enter a new name and choose New example.
Wait for the created-workspace confirmation and empty file list.
steps.why: An owned example stores your files separately from the supplied application source.
steps.note: You will create a separate editable workspace. This example is named pilot-icepack-script-1118.

steps.title: 3. Select both Python files
instructions: Choose script files. In your file picker select run.py and validate_dataset.py, then choose Open.
The script picker changes from zero to two selected files.
You are ready to import the script and its validator.
steps.why: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.
steps.expected: Selected files are not saved until you import them.
steps.note: Keep both Python files in the same example. Files are selected first; importing saves them.

steps.title: 4. Import the scripts
instructions: Choose Import script files.
Wait for Imported run.py, validate_dataset.py. Files are saved.
The file selector now contains the runnable Python script.
steps.why: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.
steps.expected: The file selector now contains the runnable script.
steps.note: If your example already contains run.py, enable Replace existing script files first. Replace only the existing files you intend to update.

steps.title: 5. Use run.py as the entry point
instructions: Set Run target to run.py.
The validator checks JSON schema, model, units and bounds before the scientific libraries are imported.
steps.why: Run target selects the entry script; other imported files can act as helpers.
steps.expected: The validator checks the JSON before loading the scientific libraries.
steps.note: Importing files does not launch a run.

steps.title: 6. Select the JSON configuration
instructions: In Datasets select icepack-shelf-small-v1.json.
If it is not listed yet, add it with Choose data files → Upload first.
Choose Reference in example.
Read the reference confirmation.
At launch, the JSON is copied to data/icepack-shelf-small-v1.json for the script to read.
steps.why: Select the dataset that this script will reference and read at launch. A reference stages this dataset under data/ when the selected example launches.
steps.note: This workflow uses JSON configuration; gridded initial fields have their own tutorial. The script reads data/icepack-shelf-small-v1.json. The reference belongs to this workspace example.

steps.title: 7. Understand the short experiment
instructions: The domain is 10 km × 10 km with 4 × 4 subdivisions and CG1 thickness/velocity.
The script runs a diagnostic solve, one 0.01-year step, then another diagnostic solve.
steps.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
steps.expected: One 0.01-year step; temperature 253.15 K; zero accumulation.
steps.note: Temperature is 253.15 K; accumulation is zero.

steps.title: 8. Review the cloud configuration
instructions: Choose Review & Launch. Check the model, workspace example, run.py target and resources.
Choose Launch cloud run when the readiness checks are ready.
This confirmation starts the run.
The new run card names pilot-icepack-script-1118.
Allow it to finish, then open View results.
steps.why: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission. This confirmation stages the reviewed inputs and starts a paid cloud job. Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
steps.expected: The native job used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB.
steps.note: You should be reviewing the custom script example. Control guide; the following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run. The native job used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB.

steps.title: 9. Open the completed native results
instructions: The job completed successfully with exit code 0.
Open Results for this custom script run.
steps.why: A completed native job and its recorded provenance provide execution evidence.
steps.expected: Submission → start: 220.087 s; task: 48.192 s; script: 15.6633 s.
steps.note: Submission → Batch start: 220.087 s; task: 48.192 s; script: 15.6633 s.

steps.title: 10. Render a saved field
instructions: Results opens with an initial preview. Select a field and use Render when needed.
This native export has 25 vertices and 32 triangles.
Thickness and velocity are finite CG1 fields; accumulation is zero.
steps.why: The solution, field name, units and mesh counts identify what you are viewing.
steps.expected: 25 vertices / 32 triangles; finite CG1 thickness and velocity.
steps.note: Use the displayed field name and units. Velocity is in metres/year; thickness is in metres.

steps.title: 11. Inspect the final thickness
instructions: Open the full saved thickness figure.
Thickness is 300.023425–499.981468 m, with area-weighted mean 400.006923 m.
steps.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
steps.note: Keep the original scientific PNG with your results.

steps.title: 12. Inspect speed and direction
instructions: Colour shows speed and arrows show direction.
The domain RMS speed is 130.141951 m/year; independent field integration agrees with the script metric.
steps.why: The unchanged saved figure preserves the complete map, axes and colour scale.
steps.expected: Domain RMS speed: 130.141951 m/year; arrows show direction.
steps.note: The figure is the unchanged downloaded archive member.

steps.title: 13. Save your result archive
instructions: Choose Download results, then open the fresh HTTPS link.
Save the 11-member ZIP containing fields, mesh, figures, metrics and runtime/RNG provenance.
steps.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
steps.expected: Keep it with your script, validator and JSON.
steps.note: Keep the ZIP with your script, validator and JSON. Use the current run’s generated link.

steps.title: What this example establishes
instructions: The initial velocity guess rises from 100 to 200 m/year; 200 is not an imposed outflow speed.
This one-step fixture has no damage field or transient time axis. Its retained output checks are separate from an independent native repeat or accuracy assessment.
steps.why: Keep the scientific input definitions and numerical qualifications with the result.
steps.expected: The 100→200 m/year initial guess is not an imposed outflow speed.
steps.note: The supplied script, validator and JSON were bound to the accepted native run.
